subject: Computer Networking
title: Web3 and Decentralization
description: A short lesson to help you apply Web3 and Decentralization.

hook.text: Web1 was read-only. Web2 let users create content. Web3 promises user ownership via blockchain.

buildup.text: Web3 uses smart contracts on Ethereum and other chains. Apps run on decentralized networks, not company servers.

discovery.text: Users own their data and digital assets as tokens. No central authority controls access or content.

twist.text: In practice, Web3 relies on centralized services: Infura for nodes, OpenSea for NFTs, MetaMask for wallets.

climax.text: Scalability and UX remain major hurdles. Gas fees and seed phrases confuse mainstream users.

punchline.text: Web3 envisions a user-owned internet. The reality is still evolving.

details.summary: Web3 envisions a decentralized internet built on blockchain technology, where users control their own data and identity without relying on centralized platforms. Smart contracts execute code on distributed networks.
details.whyItMatters: Web3 represents one vision of the internet's future where power shifts from platforms to users. Understanding its promises and limitations helps evaluate whether it will reshape the web.
takeaways: Web3 builds applications on decentralized blockchain networks
Users control their data and identity through crypto wallets
Smart contracts execute trustless logic without central servers

faq.question: How does Web3 differ from the current web?
faq.answer: The current web relies on centralized servers, platforms, and databases controlled by companies. Web3 stores data on distributed blockchains, authenticates users with crypto wallets instead of passwords, and uses smart contracts instead of centralized backend logic.

faq.question: What are the challenges facing Web3?
faq.answer: Blockchain transactions are slow and expensive compared to traditional databases. User experience is complex with wallets and gas fees. Scalability remains a fundamental challenge. Regulatory uncertainty, energy consumption concerns, and speculation in token markets complicate mainstream adoption.
